clue.text: Foreman resurrecting concealed back access route to site?

indicators.note: back says the hidden run is then read in the opposite direction, from right to left
concealed says the letters lie hidden inside the run of words Foreman resurrecting

explanation.surface: A boxer called Foreman comes back from the dead via some secret rear entrance to a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreman' looks like a person or a site boss; the answer lies backwards across 'forEMAN RESUrrecting', with 'concealed' and 'back' as the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A login name is what a user types to get into a website, so it is a cryptic route of access to a site.

clue.text: Bolshie rising at top of colliery yard

indicators.note: in a down clue, at top of places the first piece above the rest

parts.note: rising means up, as in getting up out of bed
a colliery is a coal mine, a pit

explanation.surface: A militant miner stirs up trouble at the head of the colliery yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for awkward and rebellious, close in sense to arrogantly self-assertive.

clue.text: Blast coming up from Scots University lecturer

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: frae is the Scots word for from

explanation.surface: An outburst comes from a Scottish university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' applies only to the Scots word, which is turned before the two abbreviations are added below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a sharp telling-off, and to get a sound scolding is to receive a lengthy one.

clue.text: Level unconsecrated building?

definitions.meaning: a level is a step or degree on a scale
a building not consecrated is cryptically not a church

explanation.surface: A deconsecrated building is levelled.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the usual abbreviation for church, so NOT + CH is a place not consecrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving up a notch is going up a level, a step on a scale of degree.

clue.text: Sun now? Not so much this season!

definitions.text: Sun now? Not so much this season!

parts.words: Sun now? Not so much this season!
parts.note: if today is Sunday, the next day is coming soon; and this rainy season has little sunshine

explanation.surface: A weather remark: sunshine now, but not much of it at this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Sun as Sunday: if it is Sun now, Mon is soon. The rainy season also lacks sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The wet season of South Asia brings heavy rain and little sunshine, so not much sun this season.

clue.text: Figure in live TV event, perhaps marathon

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast, a live television event shown from a location
a marathon is an example of something long

explanation.surface: A shape appears in some live televised event, a marathon perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, outside broadcast, is common British television jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is a geometric figure, the shape so named.

clue.text: Headgear needed when tipping a canine toilet into lake

indicators.note: tipping means dumping the following items out
into says those dumped items go inside the lake

parts.note: Bala is a lake in North Wales
C is the dental abbreviation for a canine tooth
lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone tipping a dog's toilet into a lake would want a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The lake is Bala in North Wales; C for canine comes from dental notation. 'tipping' and 'into' together say the three pieces are dumped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen hood covering head and neck, leaving the face partly open, is a type of headgear.

clue.text: Red top involved in hacking phone data heartlessly — this issue taken on by Guardian?

definitions.text: this issue taken on by Guardian?

indicators.note: involved in places that letter inside the rearranged mix
hacking suggests cutting up, so the letters are chopped about
heartlessly removes the middle letters of the word data
top picks the first letter of the word Red

parts.note: red top is also British slang for a tabloid newspaper, misdirecting from the letter pick

explanation.surface: A tabloid takes part in phone hacking, a story the Guardian newspaper then pursues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips the middle AT; 'hacking' then makes OPHANED, and 'involved in' slips the R inside. The surface recalls the 2011 phone-hacking scandal the Guardian exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A child left without parents may be placed with a legal guardian, who takes such offspring on.

clue.text: Collective inheritance goes regularly on pole dancing

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of goes
dancing sets the letters of on pole moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Talk of an inherited trait for pole dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes GE from GOES; 'dancing' turns ON POLE into NEPOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The total stock of genes in a population is what its members inherit between them.

clue.text: Virtuous sailor wouldn't do this

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning virtuous
a rating is an ordinary seaman in the navy

explanation.surface: A good seaman would never turn to piracy.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay spells a virtuous sailor, and the whole clue says such a sailor would not do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbing ships at sea is the act no upright seaman would commit.

clue.text: Prince, half-gone, wearing child's T-shirt?

indicators.note: wearing says the remainder is dressed in the outer word

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: half-gone says half the name is dropped, keeping the rest

parts.note: Prince Philip, the late Duke of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A prince, half-dressed, has on a child's T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Philip was the Queen's husband; 'half-gone' keeps the last three letters of his name, and 'wearing' dresses them in the child.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is an example of a garment pulled on easily without fastenings.

clue.text: Cut dressmaker's essentials up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: pins are a dressmaker's basic tools

explanation.surface: Cut the dressmaker's essentials short.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors.

clue.text: Try to land

definitions.meaning: in rugby a try is scored by grounding the ball over the line
for an aircraft, to land is to come down onto the runway

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt a landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby's try evolved from the American football score, and aircraft come down onto a runway on landing.

clue.text: He refuses to comment on parking — press seen as anti-motorist

parts.note: someone who clams up says nothing, so is a clam

explanation.surface: A spokesman says no comment on parking while the press brand him anti-motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers; it is the definition, a gripping device, and a wheel clamp is the bane of drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a device that grips by pressing, and wheel clamps immobilise illegally parked cars.

clue.text: Like pride?

definitions.meaning: like means for example, such as
pride is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for example, and split differently it says pride is one deadly sin.

clue.text: Clingy relatives tending at first to stay within vision

indicators.note: to stay within puts these pieces inside the word for vision

parts.note: sight is vision
kin are relatives

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of tending

explanation.surface: Family members on nursing duty keep each other in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that cling closely to the body are tight against the skin.

clue.text: Mix in lead with old inactive ingredient

indicators.note: in places the mixing word inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
to lace a drink is to mix something into it

explanation.surface: A recipe: stir lead in with some old, inert ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill has no active drug in it, so it is an inert component given in trials.

clue.text: Ghastly, cultivated-sounding tones

indicators.note: sounding says the word for cultivated is heard, not spelt

parts.note: grew means cultivated, as crops
so and me are two notes of the sol-fa scale, so tones

explanation.surface: Pretentious, cultivated tones of voice are awful.
explanation.walkthrough: SO and ME are tonic sol-fa notes, joined here as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ghastly is horrific and repellent, the sense of grisly horror.

clue.text: Petites amies perhaps — they may provide assistance to artists

definitions.meaning: French for little girlfriends, read cryptically as small female pals, pal plus the diminutive ending -ette

definitions.text: they may provide assistance to artists
definitions.meaning: painters mix colours on a hand-held board

explanation.surface: French girlfriends might help artists out.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's mixing board holds the paints, so it assists artists at work.

clue.text: Call outside own area may principally rely on this

definitions.text: Call outside own area may principally rely on this

indicators.note: outside puts the word for call around those letters

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

indicators.note: principally takes the leading letters of own, area and may

explanation.surface: A phone call made beyond your home network depends on this.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile phones use partner networks when abroad, letting calls work outside the home network.

clue.text: Grassed mounts for herd animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounts says the word climbs, read from the bottom

parts.note: to grass is to inform, and an informer has sung

explanation.surface: Horses put out to grass for herds of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grassed' looks like grazing; it is slang for informing to police.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest roam the African plains in vast herds.

clue.text: Thick crusts from Native-American bread

indicators.note: thick crusts means two letters at each end of the hyphenated word are kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: Taking thick-crusted loaves from a Native American baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick crusts' means two letters from each end, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: This leavened flatbread, baked in a tandoor, is a staple of South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Agreement on nothing but breaking with certainty

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places what follows below the first piece

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
O is the zero, nothing

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of but are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Agreeing on nothing, apart from a breakthrough.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means surely, said when something is beyond question.

clue.text: About to go for drop of rum during excursion? Stop drinking

indicators.note: to go for means the letter for About is swapped for the opening of rum
during places the swap within the word for an excursion

parts.note: a day out is an excursion, a coach trip for example

explanation.surface: A drunk on a day trip is told to give up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A (about, as in a-hunting) is replaced by R, the 'drop of rum', its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up alcohol after heavy drinking is to go through a period of abstinence.

clue.text: A southern bird following trawler?

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A southern seabird trails a fishing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind a vessel is the nautical sense, so something trailing a fishing boat lies in that position.

clue.text: Dismiss English judge in front of European court

indicators.note: in front of puts those letters before the rest

explanation.surface: An English judge is thrown out before a European court.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone out forcibly is to remove or expel them.

clue.text: Possessing mines, perhaps, or pits?

definitions.meaning: mines are weapons, so having them is being armed
armpits are the hollows beneath the shoulders

explanation.surface: Questioning whether pits hold mines or whether ownership is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means armed and ready, and as one word names the armpits.

clue.text: Less than half punch left, containing orange juice and wine

indicators.note: containing puts the juice inside what remains

parts.note: sangria is a Spanish wine punch; what is left after losing its first four letters is under half of it, the final three

explanation.surface: A little punch left, with orange juice and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than half punch left' keeps the last three of the seven letters of the Spanish punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from northern Spain, named after its region.

clue.text: Cut to mature better?

definitions.meaning: a power cut is a loss of supply
cryptically to age more than another

explanation.surface: Pruning to help something ripen better.
explanation.definitionFit: A power failure is a period when the electricity supply is lost.

clue.text: Way for French to reverse possibly toxic atmosphere in troubled grouping

indicators.note: to reverse says the French word is read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way
ozone is a gas that is toxic in high concentrations

explanation.surface: France's route out of the poisonous mood in a struggling alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2011 the single-currency bloc was in crisis, hence 'troubled'.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of EU states sharing the single currency was a troubled alliance in the debt crisis.

clue.text: It sounds easy in Hollywood to take in foolish star with fake

indicators.note: to take in puts the jumbled letters inside
it sounds signals letters said aloud
in American speech Z is zee, so E and Z said together give the word easy

parts.note: the simple word said aloud

indicators.note: foolish says the letters of star are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hollywood makes it easy to take in a foolish star with fakery.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say Z as zee, so the two letters together are heard as easy; 'foolish' scrambles the star and 'to take in' puts it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means substitute or imitation, a poor replacement for the real thing.

clue.text: Get into difficulties with compound of nitrates

indicators.note: a chemical compound combines things, so the letters of nitrates are recombined

explanation.surface: A chemist gets into trouble with a nitrate compound.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict someone's means puts them in hardship, as in straitened circumstances.
